issues.failure_explanation: On boundary faces the paper defines {v}=v, so the sum over all faces includes boundary contributions with full weight h_K|w|^2, while interior faces contribute with factor 1/2 (from |{w}|^2 ≤ (|w_1|^2+|w_2|^2)/2). The displayed inequality halves the boundary contributions as well and is false in general: for a one-element mesh it reads h_K||w||^2_{0,∂K} ≤ (1/2)h_K||w||^2_{0,∂K}. The correct bound has no factor 1/2, so the cross-term constant is μ_0^{-1}η^{-1/2}C̃ rather than μ_0^{-1}(2η)^{-1/2}C̃, and coercivity (positivity of C_0 = 1−κ and C_1 = μ_1^{-1}−κ) then requires η > max{1,μ_1^2}C̃^2/μ_0^2, twice the threshold stated in lemma:stability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the factor 1/2 in the face-to-element sum (boundary faces carry weight 1), propagate the resulting √2 through the cross-term estimates, and double the penalty threshold to η > max{1,μ_1^2}C̃^2/μ_0^2 in lemma:stability, lem:added-1, lem:added-2, prop:added-1, thm:added-2 and theorem4.2.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient penalty condition η > max{1,μ_1^2}C̃^2/(2μ_0^2) used in lemma:stability and assumed in the boundedness, strong-convexity, existence/uniqueness, and error-estimate results is not justified by the proofs as written; all statements carrying this explicit threshold inherit the unjustified constant.
issues.title: Face-sum estimate with factor 1/2 fails on boundary faces, corrupting the penalty threshold
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local constant fix; the method, every qualitative conclusion, the convergence rates, and the advertised 'sufficiently large penalty' scope all survive unchanged—only an explicit sufficient constant is corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:

$\epsilon_0 - m - (m+1/4)\varepsilon>0$ and $\min\{C_0, C_1\} > \varepsilon/4$.
Since $\Omega$ is a bounded domain, using the uniform boundedness of $\Eb_h$ and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have constants $C_{Eb},C_{Ehb}>0$ such that

Assume \eqref{eqn1.other}, $m<\epsilon_0$ and $\eta > \max\{1,\mu_1^2\}\,\tilde{C}^2/(2\,\mu_0^2)$. If $\Eb_h\in \Vb_h$ is a solution of the problem \eqref{eqn1.18}, then $\|\Eb_h\|_h$ is uniformly bounded with respect to the mesh size $h$.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement assumes only mesh regularity, regularity of E, and the penalty condition. The proof, however, (i) absorbs (1+ε)m||E_I−E_h||_0^2 into ε_0||E_I−E_h||_0^2 using m<ε_0, (ii) estimates the ψ^0 terms via (eqn1.other2) and (eqn1.other)(d), and (iii) uses the uniform h-boundedness of E_h, which by lem:added-1 requires (eqn1.other) and m<ε_0; existence and uniqueness of E_h (thm:added-2) also need them. None of these hypotheses appears in the theorem, so as stated it can be invoked in regimes (m ≥ ε_0) where the proof fails.

failure_location.quote: Let $\Eb$ and $\Eb_h$ be the solutions of \eqref{eqn1.1} and \eqref{eqn1.18}, respectively. Assume $\Eb \in \Hb_0(\curlb; \Omega) \cap \Hb^{s+1/2}(\Omega)$ and $\nabla\times \Eb \in \Hb^s(\Omega)$, $s > 1/2$. Choose the penalty constant $\eta > \max\{1,\mu_1^2\}\,\tilde{C}^2/(2\,\mu_0^2)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the assumptions (eqn1.other) and m<ε_0 to the hypotheses of theorem4.2, exactly as done in lem:added-1, lem:added-2 and thm:added-2; the paper itself notes m<ε_0 is always achievable by taking the time step k sufficiently small.
issues.overall_effect: The main a priori error estimate is stated without the structural and smallness hypotheses under which it is proved; without m<ε_0 the absorption step, the uniform bound on E_h, and even the existence/uniqueness of E_h are unsupported.
issues.title: Theorem 4.2 omits the hypotheses (eqn1.other) and m<ε₀ that its proof explicitly uses
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis already assumed verbatim in every neighbouring result is a local condition that leaves the method, the estimate, the rate, and the advertised scope fully intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, if $\Eb \in \Hb_0(\curlb; \Omega) \cap \Hb^{s+1}(\Omega)$ for some number $s > 0$, then

if $\Eb\in\Hb_0(\curlb;\Omega)\cap\Hb^{3/2}(\Omega)$ and $\nabla\times \Eb \in \Hb^1(\Omega)$, we have the optimal linear convergence order:
\[\| \Eb-\Eb_h\|_h \leq C\,h.\]

issues.failure_explanation: The squared energy-norm bound (eqn:error bound) contains the first-power term (C_{Eb}+C_{Ehb})||E−E_I||_0, so the final rate is governed by ||E−Π_N E||_0^{1/2}. To get the claimed h^{(min{s,l}+1)/2} the proof invokes (eqn:lemma4-3), whose hypothesis is E ∈ H^{s+1}(Ω), but the theorem only assumes E ∈ H^{s+1/2}(Ω). Under the stated regularity the Nédélec L^2-error is only O(h^{min{s+1/2,l+1}}) in general (e.g., s=1, l=1 with E ∈ H^{3/2}\H^2 gives O(h^{3/2}), not O(h^2), by the L^2 best-approximation barrier), so the argument yields only O(h^{(s+1/2)/2}) for s ≤ l. Hence the stated rate, and in particular the corollary 'E ∈ H^{3/2}, ∇×E ∈ H^1 ⇒ ||E−E_h||_h ≤ Ch', are not proved.

failure_location.quote:
Applying the error bounds \eqref{energy norm estimate} and \eqref{eqn:lemma4-3}, we derive from \eqref{eqn:error bound} that
\[
\|\Eb_I-\Eb_h\|_h\leq C\,h^{(\min\{s,l\}+1)/2}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the regularity hypothesis to E ∈ H_0(curl;Ω) ∩ H^{s+1}(Ω) (which also yields ∇×E ∈ H^s(Ω)); the same proof then legitimately applies (eqn:lemma4-3) and gives ||E−E_h||_h ≤ C h^{(min{s,l}+1)/2} whenever min{s,l} ≥ 1, in particular optimal first order for linear elements with E ∈ H^2(Ω) — the corollary's H^{3/2} assumption must be raised to H^2, and for 1/2 < s < 1 the exponent must be weakened to min{s,(s+1)/2} = s.
issues.overall_effect: The a priori error estimate of theorem4.2 and the advertised optimal first-order convergence for linear elements under H^{3/2} regularity are unsupported as stated; consequently the abstract/introduction claims of optimal convergence order under 'suitable regularity' hold only in a stronger regularity regime than the paper advertises. The numerical example (smooth reference solution) is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed convergence rate in Theorem 4.2 is not supported under the stated H^{s+1/2} regularity
issues.why_classification: No new proof architecture is needed—the existing argument goes through once the regularity is raised by half a derivative, and the headline result (optimal first-order convergence of low-order IPDG) survives. However, the repair necessarily withdraws the advertised low-regularity regime (first-order convergence under H^{3/2}), a limited weakening of the stated scope that is more than a routine local fix but leaves a recognizably comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: The stopping test at loop index l requires λ_h^{l−1}, but the algorithm initializes only E_h^0; λ_h^l is defined inside the loop (λ_h^l ∈ ω(|E_h^{l−1}|)∂|E_h^l|), so λ_h^0 is never defined. At the first iteration (l=1) the termination criterion references a nonexistent quantity and divides by its norm, so the procedure as written cannot execute its own stopping test at l=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Initialize the multiplier before the loop, e.g., choose any selection λ_h^0 ∈ ω(|E_h^0|)∂|E_h^0| (or set λ_h^0 = 0 and apply the λ-part of the stopping test only from l = 2 onward).
issues.overall_effect: The iterative algorithm used to produce all numerical results is not fully specified: its termination behaviour at the first iteration is undefined.
issues.title: Uzawa stopping criterion references the never-initialized multiplier λ_h^0
issues.why_classification: A one-line initialization makes the procedure well-defined; no theorem, convergence guarantee, or numerical claim of the paper is affected.
